# forgesworn/anvil

> Forge-hardened release tool for JS/TS libraries. Multi-runner
> reproducible-build attestation, OIDC trusted publishing, SLSA
> provenance, pre-publish secret scan, exports-map check, frozen-vector
> gate, runtime-only npm audit, action-pin auditing. Pure bash, ~1600
> lines, auditable in thirty minutes.

## What this is

A GitHub Action (reusable workflow + composite fallback) that publishes
npm packages with hard pre-publish gates. Zero dependencies, pure bash,
auditable in thirty minutes.

The flagship feature: two parallel CI builds on independent runners must
produce byte-identical tarballs, or the release is blocked. No other
JS release tool offers this today.

## Who it's for

Any JavaScript/TypeScript library author who publishes to npm and wants
a release pipeline with fewer moving parts than the library it ships.
Especially useful for libraries where a compromised publish would matter
-- authentication, payments, cryptography, infrastructure -- but the
gates are valuable for any package.

## How to use it

Five-line caller workflow in your library's `.github/workflows/release.yml`:

```yaml
name: release
on:
  release:
    types: [published]
permissions:
  contents: write
  id-token: write
jobs:
  release:
    uses: forgesworn/anvil/.github/workflows/release.yml@v0
    with:
      vector-test-command: npm run test:vectors
```

Configure npm trusted publishing on npmjs.com for YOUR repo and YOUR
caller workflow file (not forgesworn/anvil). Bump package.json,
tag, push, create a GitHub Release. The workflow handles everything
else.

## Architecture

The reusable workflow runs as a four-job DAG:

- **build-a**: all gates (tag match, tests, vectors, audit, exports,
  secrets, action pins) then npm pack with normalised mtimes
- **build-b**: parallel build + pack on a second runner
- **reproduce**: compare sha256s; strict mode blocks on mismatch
- **publish**: upload the canonical tarball to npm, update the GitHub
  Release body with an artefact-integrity block, upload the tarball as
  a release asset

## Step scripts

All in `steps/`, all bash, all sourcing `lib.sh` for shared helpers:

| Script | Purpose |
|---|---|
| verify-tag.sh | Git tag matches package.json version |
| run-tests.sh | Full test suite |
| verify-vectors.sh | Frozen-vector gate |
| verify-audit.sh | npm audit --omit=dev |
| verify-exports.sh | Every exports subpath exists on disk |
| verify-secrets.sh | Secret scan over pack set |
| verify-action-pins.sh | Warn/fail on unpinned uses: in workflows |
| normalise-mtimes.sh | Touch all files to SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH |
| record-tarball.sh | npm pack, hash, write tarball.meta |
| compare-tarball-meta.sh | Reproducibility gate (compare two metas) |
| publish-npm.sh | Publish the exact recorded tarball via OIDC |
| publish-jsr.sh | JSR publish if jsr.json exists |
| update-release.sh | CHANGELOG extraction, integrity block, asset upload |
| changelog-extract.sh | Parse CHANGELOG.md for the version section |
| lib.sh | Shared helpers (header, log, warn, die, require_cmds) |

## Exports-map check (verify-exports.sh)

Catches the "I deleted src/foo.ts but forgot to update exports" class of
bug before it ships a broken import to downstream consumers. Neither
`publint` nor `arethetypeswrong` perform this file-existence check.

### What it validates

**Modern exports field:** Uses jq to walk the entire `.exports` tree in
`package.json`, including all conditional keys (`import`, `require`,
`types`, `node`, `browser`, `default`), nested conditionals, and string
shorthand. Every leaf string starting with `./` is treated as a path
that must exist on disk.

**Legacy entry points:** Also checks top-level `main`, `module`,
`types`, `typings`, and `bin` (both string and object forms). These are
the pre-exports world but still shipped to consumers. Paths without a
`./` prefix are normalised automatically.

Duplicate paths (e.g. when `default` repeats an `import` target) are
deduplicated so each file is checked exactly once.

### Configuration

No special configuration required. The check runs automatically as part
of the build-a job. The only relevant input is `package-json` (defaults
to `package.json`) which controls the path to the manifest file.

### How it enforces the gate

- If any exported path does not exist on disk, the step exits with
  status 1 and the release is blocked.
- Output on failure: `warning: missing: ./dist/missing.js` for each
  missing path, then `error: N exports targets missing on disk —
  refusing to publish`.
- Output on success: `ok  ./dist/index.js` for each path, then
  `ok: all N export targets exist`.
- If no exports or legacy entry points are declared, the check warns
  and passes (exit 0).

### Example package.json triggering the check

```json
{
  "exports": {
    ".": {
      "import": "./dist/index.mjs",
      "require": "./dist/index.cjs",
      "types": "./dist/index.d.ts"
    },
    "./utils": {
      "import": "./dist/utils.mjs",
      "require": "./dist/utils.cjs"
    }
  },
  "main": "./dist/index.cjs",
  "types": "./dist/index.d.ts"
}
```

All six paths (four from exports, two from legacy main/types) must exist
after the build step. If `./dist/utils.mjs` is missing, the release is
blocked.

## Key inputs (reusable workflow)

| Input | Default | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| node-version | 24.11.0 | Node version (must ship npm >= 11.5.x for OIDC; 22 LTS ships 10.9.x which is too old) |
| registry-url | https://registry.npmjs.org | npm registry URL |
| test-command | npm test | Full test suite command |
| vector-test-command | (empty) | Frozen-vector gate command (skip if empty) |
| changelog-file | CHANGELOG.md | Path to changelog |
| package-json | package.json | Path to package.json |
| audit-level | low | npm audit threshold (low/moderate/high/critical) |
| version-strategy | manual | manual: you bump and tag; verify: also checks conventional commits match your bump |
| reproducibility-mode | strict | strict: block on mismatch; warn: log only; off: skip build-b and reproduce jobs entirely |
| strict-action-pins | true | Fail on unpinned `uses:` refs in consumer workflows |
| dry-run | false | Skip real publish |
| debug | false | Diagnostic logging for OIDC issues |

The composite action (`uses: forgesworn/anvil@v0`) accepts the
same inputs but does not include the reproducible-build gate (build-b
and reproduce jobs). Use the reusable workflow for full protection.

Composite action callers must add `actions/checkout` before the step
(the reusable workflow handles checkout internally):

```yaml
jobs:
  release:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: write
      id-token: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: forgesworn/anvil@v0
        with:
          vector-test-command: npm run test:vectors
```

For JSR dual-publish via the reusable workflow, pass the JSR token as
a secret:

```yaml
jobs:
  release:
    uses: forgesworn/anvil/.github/workflows/release.yml@v0
    secrets:
      JSR_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.JSR_TOKEN }}
```
